title: CBI Books Kishore Biyani, Future Retail in Rs 904 Crore SBI Fraud Case
excerpt: India's Central Bureau of Investigation registered the case on November 4 on a State Bank of India complaint and searched premises linked to Future Retail's promoters in Mumbai on Friday, alleging loan funds were diverted through associate companies.
body:
• The CBI has booked Future Retail Ltd, Kishore Biyani and Rakesh Biyani over an alleged wrongful loss of Rs 904.32 crore to State Bank of India.
  • The case, registered on November 4, follows an SBI complaint alleging credit facilities from a consortium of nine banks were not used for their sanctioned purpose.
  • Investigators searched multiple premises linked to the promoters and directors in Mumbai on Friday and said incriminating documents were recovered and seized.
  • For investors and lenders, the allegations are unproven: the FIR starts a criminal investigation, and Biyani did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

India's Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has registered a bank fraud case against Future Retail Ltd and its promoters Kishore Biyani and Rakesh Biyani, alleging a wrongful loss of Rs 904.32 crore to the State Bank of India (SBI), the agency said on Friday. Reuters put the amount at 9.04 billion rupees, or about $96.01 million.

Rakesh Biyani and his cousin Kishore Biyani are top executives of Future Retail, the company behind retail outlets including Big Bazaar, according to The Hindu BusinessLine. The CBI said the two have been booked on charges of criminal conspiracy in connection with bank loans received by the company.

Searches in Mumbai after November 4 registration

After registering the case on November 4, the CBI conducted searches on Friday at multiple premises linked to the promoters and directors of Future Retail in Mumbai. The agency said incriminating documents relevant to the investigation were recovered during the searches.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=v4P_dVb2PcI

Apart from the Biyanis and their company, the CBI has also named unknown public servants and unknown others as accused in the FIR. The agency said that would allow names to be added in a chargesheet if the probe produces evidence against additional persons.

Reuters reported that Biyani did not immediately respond to its request for comment.

What SBI has alleged

The CBI acted on a complaint filed by SBI. According to the agency, the accused entered into a criminal conspiracy and obtained credit facilities such as working capital, term loans and letters of credit from a consortium of nine banks, including SBI.

The company availed credit facilities from SBI's Commercial Branch at Fort, Mumbai, but, the CBI alleged, defrauded the bank by not utilising the funds for the intended purpose for which they were sanctioned. It alleged the company diverted the funds by siphoning them off through associate companies and connected entities, causing loss to the bank.

Future Retail operated multiple retail formats across hypermarkets and supermarkets, including Big Bazaar, Fashion@Big Bazaar and Foodhall. It was also engaged in general trading of FMCG and fashion goods through the stores it operated.

What happens next

The investigation is continuing to ascertain the full extent of the alleged conspiracy, identify the role of all involved persons, including public servants and private individuals, and trace the end use of the loan funds, the CBI said.

The case adds a criminal investigation to Future Retail's long financial collapse. Reuters noted that the Mumbai bench of the National Company Law Tribunal had ordered the liquidation of Future Retail in 2024.

For diaspora investors who once held Future Group stocks or followed Big Bazaar as a bellwether of Indian organised retail, the immediate takeaway is procedural rather than conclusive: an FIR and searches mark the start of a probe, not a finding of guilt, and the next material milestones will be any chargesheet, arrests or court filings that test SBI's diversion allegation with documents.
